title: Helping a ragged girl met on a bus
summary: A story of giving clothes to a poor girl and her mother, offered as an example of her being blessed.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now later I met a girl on the bus -- can I tell you this?

On the bus one day, I was going up to my other apartment. And this little girl -- this girl, she wasn't a little girl, big fat girl, sitting there -- this last winter. Cold, it was so cold. And she was just ragged. Her clothes looked so bad, and I felt so sorry for her. And I went over to her and I said, 'Miss, excuse me, but will you

accept -- take what I'm giving you and not get angry?" She said, what is it? And I said, "I'm a nurse, and sometimes a lot of us nurses get together." And I said, "We get a lot of nice things together, and maybe they stop us from wearing them, and we don't want to throw them away, we want to give them to people, some worthy person." And I said, "Would you accept some things if I get them and send them to you?" And she said, yes. She had books in her arms, I guess she was on her way to school.

So I said, "Well, what is your address? What's your name and what's your address?" She wrote it down, her address and everything. And I sent her a box out of this world. And her mother -- oh, and I said, "Now, you show this letter -- you tell your mother that a lady spoke to you on the bus, so she'll know if a Miss Hunter calls, it will be me." So she said, "Well, we haven't got a telephone." So I said, "Well, I'm going to write you a letter." I said, "What's your mother's name." She told me. I said, "Put your mother's and father's name in there so I can write to them, so they'll know. And I did. And I wrote them a letter, and I told them about these clothes, before I sent the box. And I put my phone number in there.
And the mother called me. And so when the mother called me, then I knew it was all right, see. So I sent her this box, and in the meantime I met her mother again, and I

gave her mother another box, and yesterday the mother called me and was talking to me. And I asked her what the girl wanted for Christmas, and what the girl's size was. And she told me size 18, because she's a big fat girl. And so I wasn't in a humor to talk, so I told her I was getting ready to go to work, but I'd call her.

So I called her this morning, and I told her that I had to go up to Hip Monday, and for her to see me at Hip (PHONETIC) Monday. She lives right around the corner from Hip, according to the address, and come into Dr. Alsop's office and ask for me, and that I would give her some money to buy her daughter some clothes. Which I'm going to do.
Well. But I get back so many blessings. Look at this, this is a blessing.
Yeah, but it's something you brought on yourself.
Yeah, but it's a blessing, Chris. A lot of people do good things, but they don't get these blessings. And I'm blessed, see, so I'm going to give her money to buy that girl some clothes for Christmas.
